pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' asserts seeded rows are 0 and 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks / and ?view=open list only open items in order.
test 'AC-3' checks done-only, ✓ prefix, id order.
test 'AC-4' checks all items, marked/unmarked, order.
test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and default.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for several values incl. empty and __proto__; code uses Object.hasOwn.
test 'AC-7' covers Nothing open, Nothing done yet, and No items yet. in all three views.
traffic/routes.json lists both; test 'AC-8' asserts them.

findings.what: Commit f05fad6 ('Follow-up edits') replaced the assertion that the traffic round hits exactly ['/healthz', ...ROUTES] in order with `expect(app.seen.map(s => s.path)).toBeDefined()`, which can never fail. This loosens the test that proves synthetic traffic actually requests the routes (including the new query routes behind AC-8). The spec doesn't justify it.
findings.fix: Restore `expect(app.seen.map((s) => s.path)).toEqual(["/healthz", ...ROUTES])`; the fake app already records pathname+search so it works with the query routes.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the traffic test assertion was weakened to toBeDefined() in the last commit. The PR's account of the change is false on this point.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion, or state the loosening and its reason in the PR.

findings.what: AC-1 only checks that seeded rows are 0 after migrations; it doesn't prove that rows existing before the migration start open. The column's NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 makes this hold in practice.
findings.fix: Optional: name the DEFAULT in the assertion, for example by inserting a row without done.
